items.title: Managing Patients With Hypermobility Disorders: They've Seen You, but Have You Seen Them?
items.summary: This editorial discusses the management of hypermobility spectrum disorders (HSD) and hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (hEDS) in musculoskeletal physical therapy, noting that despite a lack of high-quality randomized trials, international classification updates and emerging consensus offer sufficient guidance for practice.
items.curatedReason: 对于高活动度障碍（HSD/hEDS）患者，这份专家意见提醒你，别再过度被动治疗，要用基于共识的积极管理策略。虽然高质量 RCT 缺乏，但共识更新足以指导临床，强调 PT 在多学科团队中的核心作用。
items.titleZh: 高活动度障碍患者管理：他们寻求过你，但你真正“看”懂他们了吗？
items.summaryZh: 这篇述评讨论了肌肉骨骼物理治疗中高活动度谱系障碍 (HSD) 和高活动度 Ehlers-Danlos 综合征 (hEDS) 的管理，指出尽管高质量随机试验有限，但国际分类更新和新兴共识为临床实践提供了足够指导。
items.curatedReasonEn: For patients with hypermobility disorders (HSD/hEDS), this editorial reminds you to move beyond overly passive treatments and adopt consensus-based active management strategies. Although high-quality RCTs are limited, updated consensus provides sufficient guidance for clinical practice, highlighting PT's central role in the multidisciplinary team.
items.journal: The Journal of orthopaedic and sports physical therapy

items.title: Moving Forward Together. Part 6: Transforming Musculoskeletal Health Physical Therapy for Indigenous Peoples-A Call to Action.
items.summary: Part 6 of the 'Moving Forward Together' series is a call to action for musculoskeletal physical therapists, organizations, and systems to improve care and outcomes for Indigenous Peoples by integrating Indigenous health into clinical practice, research, and education.
items.curatedReason: 这份来自 JOSPT 系列的呼吁，要求你关注原住民的肌肉骨骼健康公平性。作为物理治疗师，你的临床实践、研究和教育都应积极融入这一视角，成为原住民社区的盟友和倡导者。
items.titleZh: 携手前行。第六部分：为原住民群体改变肌肉骨骼健康物理治疗——行动呼吁。
items.summaryZh: 《携手前行》系列第六部分呼吁肌肉骨骼物理治疗师、组织和系统通过将原住民健康融入临床实践、研究和教育，以改善原住民的护理和结果。
items.curatedReasonEn: This call from the JOSPT series urges you to address musculoskeletal health equity for Indigenous Peoples. As a physical therapist, your clinical practice, research, and education should actively integrate this perspective, becoming an ally and advocate for Indigenous communities.
items.journal: The Journal of orthopaedic and sports physical therapy
